scenes.title: The Fifth Mug
scenes.prose:
The fifth mug has spent months clipped above the table. Kai polished it once and denied doing so. Now its owner is a small moving shape on the landing camera, waiting beside relief cargo until the pad is declared clear. The player stands with Rafi at the inner airlock control. A greeting is ready, but the open command waits for two agreeing checks.

Ferreira gives her name as if this were any other handover. Rafi asks her to repeat the seal indication. She does, without a joke about rank. Beyond the camera frame, the lander's dust has settled; nothing outside billows like smoke. Cargo passes through the transfer procedure before anyone removes a glove.

Inside, Ferreira reaches for a chair, sees the four cadets waiting, and takes the corridor watch instead. The player carries her mug to the table. The commander who used to be a voice has weight, tired shoulders and a place to sleep. Aurora must now support five people, and its next ledger must say so.

scenes.title: The Watch She Takes
scenes.prose:
Ferreira's first watch is uneventful, which makes Amara suspicious. On Earth, the commander always seemed to arrive at the moment a warning sounded. Here she checks a label, writes the time and waits for the next reading. The player follows her through the corridor that felt unfamiliar in April.

A replacement relay controller sits in a sealed crate. Rafi reads its serial against the received manifest; Kai checks that the service diagram is stored locally. The spare does not fix anything simply by arriving. It needs a compatible housing, an isolation procedure and a crew who know where it is. They put those facts on the inventory board.

At the atmosphere panel, Amara finds a handwritten correction she made months earlier. Ferreira asks why it remains visible. Amara says the old number was wrong. The player compares the second gauge and signs the current reading. The panel becomes evidence of a checked mistake rather than embarrassment. Their meal begins after the handover, not after an invented emergency.

scenes.title: The Order We Left In
scenes.prose:
Four records wait under transparent weights: a relay fault report, a greenhouse service note, an evacuation order and an ascent manifest. Ferreira puts them down without arranging them. She asks the player to reconstruct the order before asking what she remembers. The task begins with timestamps and signatures, not an accusation.

One note describes a power connector already degraded. Another records the relay failure. The player distinguishes a condition from the moment it became dangerous. A photograph of frozen trays supplies a consequence but cannot date the original fault. Wrong placements remain visible long enough for their contradiction to be understood; correcting them costs no survival resource.

The ascent manifest supplies the final check. Every listed crew member boarded. The player compares the roster with the boarding record instead of inferring a death from a sad photograph. Rafi exhales before anyone speaks. An unanswered question about the seeds remains, but it has changed shape. The mystery concerns what people carried home and what they hoped someone might find later.

scenes.title: A Garden That Had Not Flowered
scenes.location: Archive images at the mission table
scenes.prose:
Mei brings the frozen-garden photographs beside Alo's preserved petal. For months she has called the room below the hatch an old garden. Now that phrase seems to compete with their first bloom. If flowers were already there, what did Alo change? The player opens the growth sheet instead of accepting either flattering explanation.

The sheet records young seedlings, curled leaves and evacuation before flowering. Close images show why a curled frozen leaf is not evidence of a flower. Mei marks what is visible and leaves an uncertain patch unlabelled. Amara checks that the board describes the documented trial, rather than pretending a photograph proves every unseen moment.

Alo's record stays separate: flower, compatible pollen from Tara, mature pods, dry-down and forty-two harvested seeds. The petal is not alive. The descendants in the present room are. By aligning two timelines, the player makes space for both expeditions without stealing either achievement. Ferreira watches Mei revise the caption. She does not ask her to make an unfinished trial sound successful.

scenes.title: What I Didn't Say
scenes.prose:
Ferreira sits where a commander would usually stand. Her hands rest without touching the records. She describes Expedition Zero's final equipment-recovery minutes: a seed drawer, a service annex already cooling, and a gardener who believed another crew would come. The vault had been placed during an earlier survey. Nobody drove into a crater while the ascent vehicle waited.

The player can ask about the retreat order or the saved seeds. Both lead to facts secured by the record. Ferreira helped the gardener board. The fault made continued habitation unsafe. Returning alive was the right action, and it still hurt to leave living work unfinished. She admits that avoiding this history made discovery feel like secrecy.

Mei does not respond by pretending the delay never mattered. She asks why the commander trusted them with equipment but not disappointment. Ferreira accepts the question. The player chooses a first response, then reads the other perspective too. This is not a forgiveness meter. A working crew can keep a disagreement visible and decide together what must happen next.

scenes.title: Two Kinds of Repair
scenes.location: Local records desk and spare locker
scenes.prose:
Kai opens the old relay diagram beside the new controller's service card. Their housings resemble one another, but he will not call them interchangeable from a picture. The player compares connector specification, isolation points and the actual spare serial. The controller remains packed. This investigation does not repair the present uplink, which is still working normally.

Across the table, Mei rewrites the unanswered question. It no longer asks whether the old expedition cared. It asks who wrote N., and whether that person wants to hear from them. The difference fits on one line and changes the conversation. Ferreira leaves the personal identity page with Rao for consented release later.

The player produces two separate products: a technical compatibility note and a respectful question for the gardener. Kai clips his note inside the crate. Mei keeps her question beside a current photograph. Neither replaces the other. Ferreira takes her mug back to the watch station. Before observation begins, the player verifies that the repair procedure opens without an Earth connection.

scenes.title: Stars Without Streaks
scenes.prose:
Kai asks where the shooting stars are. The monitor shows a dark plain and small flashes enlarged for inspection. There are no atmospheric trails above the surface. Rafi hands the player a frame-based observation log. Nobody must rush outside for a better view.

The first candidate stays at the same detector coordinate across several frames. Another appears briefly at a mapped surface location with a distinct onset. The player inspects neighbouring frames before classifying either. Amara requests a reason beside every accepted event; a lucky click cannot become a scientific report. Six genuine flashes must be verified in the teaching sequence, while two fixed artifacts are rejected.

As the list grows, the plain seems less empty. Mei says the Moon keeps marks too small to notice from their window. Ferreira reminds her that this is an amplified instrument view, not naked-eye fireworks. The player saves the sixth supported event and carries the observation clock into maintenance. Wonder has supplied a reason to look carefully, not permission to overstate what appeared.

scenes.title: Dust Has a Cost
scenes.location: Maintenance console and isolated garden spur
scenes.prose:
The observation report is ready, but Amara does not let a completed screen become a completed watch. A panel trend shows less output than its reference. A separate pressure trace suggests a small isolated branch leak. The player separates the observations first; one convenient explanation cannot account for every change.

Neither of the protective upgrades offered after this chapter has been earned yet. Scheduled cleaning must restore the panel's teaching profile, and the player must isolate and patch the damaged garden spur. A pressure-safe procedure keeps the living enclosure closed. The player predicts which trace each repair should change, then compares independent before-and-after records. A correct patch cannot be credited for an unrelated energy improvement.

Mei watches through the sealed enclosure. Nobody opens a greenhouse to vacuum to wipe a leaf. Kai jokes about dust keeping a diary, then labels the trends correctly. The crew earns a later choice of Dust Shield or Whipple protection because it now understands both failure mechanisms. Future equipment will change future maintenance; it cannot retroactively perform today's work.

scenes.title: What the Flashes Cannot Prove
scenes.prose:
Rafi places tonight's observation record beside Expedition Zero's damage report. Their dates differ, and he leaves them that way. It is tempting to make an impressive flash explain the broken relay twelve years earlier. The player can draw a line only where the evidence supports one.

The same kind of hazard explains why impact monitoring matters. It cannot establish that a specific old fault was caused by an impact, particularly when the original report describes relay failure and degraded power hardware without a verified strike. The player moves that strong claim to unsupported. Its correction stays visible in the debrief so the missing connection has a reason.

Ferreira smiles at a report containing a blank. It is the first empty space all evening that makes her feel better. Rafi saves the report without apology. Candidate frames, maintenance traces and archive chronology now form one complete investigation: observe, test, explain the limits. The player carries that discipline into the identity question. A familiar initial can be a clue. A signed page must finish the proof.

scenes.title: The Name on the Page
scenes.location: Mission table, live Earth data link
scenes.prose:
Rao's call arrives with a signed page and a permission note. The player checks its signature against the recovered manifest. N.R. is no longer an invitation to guess a name. It is Dr. Noor Rahman, the botanist who left the seeds, returned to Bangladesh and founded Last Light Academy.

Rao says she has read the crew's transmitted reports. Transmitted matters: Noor did not see through April's Earth blackout and never watched private moments through an invisible camera. The player opens the receipt list, comparing creation times with delivery after contact returned. Mei finds the first bloom photograph and the forty-two-seed harvest entry. Support has an actual information path.

Ferreira explains that Noor wanted future crews to finish a garden her own expedition left unfinished. This does not make the cadets actors in a secret test. Their repairs and decisions belonged to them. The player places the signed page beside the anonymous packet image. Only after the shared reveal does the journal expand the initials into Noor's full name.

scenes.title: An Invitation, Not an Answer Owed
scenes.location: Message composer at the mission table
scenes.prose:
The composer offers a current garden photograph and a cursor. Mei spent months wanting an answer from N. Now that the name is known, the first sentence feels harder. Kai suggests sending every graph. Amara says the graphs can be attachments. The player decides what the invitation itself should ask.

Both authored invitations leave Noor a choice. One asks whether she would like to see the next stage. The other says a place for her work remains at their table. Neither demands a reply, accuses her of abandoning anyone or turns a private history into a puzzle prize. The camera stays on Mei's hands while the player checks the text.

Rao confirms delivery through the available Earth path. No immediate voice sounds from the speaker. The crew finishes its checked report while the new relationship waits at its own pace. Ferreira places her mug beside four familiar ones. The table has not gained a magical sixth occupant. It has gained a connection to someone who may choose a later conversation.

scenes.title: One More Seed
scenes.prose:
Noor replies in text the next day. She thanks the crew for asking and would like to see what grows next. Mei pins the message where a gardener can read it without bending over the console. The player opens the approved quarantine record, not the entire seed case.

One viable cotton specimen is cleared for the indoor reference bay. Eleven other vault specimens remain protected. Amara reads those quantities aloud, then closes that ledger before opening the separate founder reserve: thirty original Alo-by-Tara seeds, still sealed. No inventory gains a seed because an album picture was unlocked.

Planting repeats the opening game's gesture with better understanding. The player labels the cassette, checks the medium and closes the pressure-safe bay. No cotton flower appears on command. A dated montage shows leaves and repeated care over subsequent weeks while Alo's descendants continue nearby. Mei places the preserved petal beside the label. It remembers an individual; the living room continues a lineage. Kai has already begun marking the guide-light circuit for January's eclipse. At chapter completion, the player selects Dust Shield or Whipple protection for later chapters, with neither option required to solve today's maintenance.

The crew rehearses a five-segment protected-service budget, records a labelled eclipse view, connects family within a valid path and receives Noor's known-sender text. scenes.title: The Lamp Is Still Here
scenes.prose:
Kai remembers the locker without needing its label. Inside is the hand light Rafi left within reach during their first night. It is scratched now, and its battery needs a measured charge. The player picks it up instead of searching for a brighter replacement. Familiar equipment carries evidence of previous use.

Ferreira arrives at the doorway and waits while Kai checks the charge. He says plainly that he is still afraid of the dark. No one calls this a failure of training. Amara adds the lamp to the protected-service plan as a small, useful load. Rafi asks whether Kai wants company during the transfer. The player chooses a companion without changing anyone's assigned responsibility.

The room does not become frightening to prove his fear real. Its ordinary hum continues while the checklist fills. Kai clips the charged lamp where both hands can remain free. His first task is complete because he has identified a need and prepared for it, not because he has stopped feeling it.

scenes.title: A Memory With a Switch
scenes.prose:
The player opens Kai's short memory beside the present circuit map. A childhood storm once left his home dark without warning. The log offers sounds and a text equivalent, not a forced frightening reenactment. Kai can stop the memory and keep every fact needed for the mission.

What frightened him was not simply a missing bulb. It was not knowing when the light would return or who had a plan. On the table, the player separates those uncertainties into questions the crew can answer: which services remain powered, what the forecast covers, and how to signal a fault. The eclipse schedule is a source-informed scenario, with local timing still awaiting verified geometry.

Rafi points to a guide-light branch that appears on every segment. Kai traces it with one finger and checks the reserve once. The animation echoes his old double-checking habit without making caution the joke. He closes the memory himself. This time the room has a map, a companion and a way to ask what happens next.

scenes.title: The Seven-Unit Promise
scenes.prose:
Five segment cards spread across the board: precharge, ingress, totality, egress and recovery. Kai places essential services beneath every card. Air circulation, minimum heat, dim growth light and the guide light travel as a protected package. The player can expand the package to see its components without making four disconnected promises.

The current rehearsal uses a labelled teaching allocation. Five essential packages, one pump preparation and one camera preparation cost seven game units altogether. They are not kilowatt-hours, and the board does not add a second elapsed-time bill. Amara checks the arithmetic against the displayed jar and return margin. The verified-data version will replace this fallback as a single model, not stack another cost on it.

Kai asks the player to predict the result before running the rehearsal. A missing package makes a specific service warning appear in its segment. Fixing it changes the forecast immediately. A correct plan is a visible relationship between choices and outcomes, not a hidden combination copied from an answer key.

Neither preview spends actual reserve. Both show the same forecast and equipment, so a change in one load has an interpretable consequence.

The floodlight plan consumes margin without helping scrubbers, return water or the filtered camera. Kai can see exactly what that brightness would cost the shared mission. Rafi does not tell him to stop wanting light. He moves the small guide light into the same corridor view. The player compares usefulness, power and the available path rather than treating every comfort as waste.

Amara asks Kai to describe the chosen compromise to Mei. Explaining it makes the decision a team promise: the room can be dim while a reliable route remains visible. The player labels the guide-light branch and disables decorative floods in the proposed schedule. Both plans remain in the debrief, allowing a later learner to see why the quieter one worked.

Its label is large enough to read and its status appears in text as well as colour. The player predicts which indicator should change before selecting the simulated disconnect.

Only the test branch drops. The protected essentials remain on, just as the diagram promised. If the player expected a complete blackout, the board traces the isolating boundary instead of merely announcing an incorrect answer. Kai reads the same route physically across the panel. Rafi rehearses the short local checkback they will use during an actual interruption.

The player restores the test branch through the approved sequence and verifies the return. The exercise ends in the same safe state in which it began. It has created no additional failure in the habitat. Ferreira checks that the rehearsal result and the actual mission readiness are distinct records. A successful simulation supports confidence, but the next scene still requires every real station check.

Kai asks each role for a short report and repeats the part his schedule depends on. The player places the matching readiness token only after its observation is acknowledged. Five time segments remain visible above four role checks. The sequence cannot be completed by repeatedly pressing a single unlabelled confirmation.

The external camera's protective configuration is checked before its image appears. Nobody looks directly into a bright Sun to prove courage. If verified local geometry is not yet available in production, the screen clearly uses the source-informed scenario view and conceptual diagram. The same engineering decisions remain meaningful. Ferreira asks whose call it is. Kai looks around the occupied work positions before answering. Readiness belongs to the crew who checked the plan, not to the loudest person in the room.

scenes.title: The Red Ring
scenes.prose:
A dark disc takes a growing bite from the camera's bright image. The player marks ingress against the displayed teaching timeline. The monitor frame stays visible; this is a protected instrument view, not an invitation to stare outside. A separate label distinguishes the verified eclipse calendar date from Aurora's still-unverified viewing geometry.

At the red-rim moment, the room becomes quiet without forcing the controls away. The player may hold the frame to inspect a conceptual Earth cross-section. Sunlight passes through the atmosphere around Earth's edge, providing the physical explanation for the colour. The diagram does not paint a geographically resolved stripe of Bangladesh onto the camera image.

Mei reaches for a poetic sentence about every sunrise and sunset. Amara leaves the sentence in the conversation, then adds the mechanism beside it. Wonder and explanation can occupy the same page. The player records the observation and checks which part is sourced astronomy, which part is a diagram, and which timing belongs to this fictional expedition. The ring becomes more interesting when its labels are honest.

The contact panel shows a valid Earth path for the authored observation window. Kai's family message is waiting at its far end. The player connects the call only after the path check; the eclipse itself is not treated as a magic radio switch. If contact is interrupted, the recording buffer preserves words rather than inventing a continuous connection.

Kai describes the small light and the plan around it. He does not claim the dark is harmless everywhere or forever. His family asks whether someone is with him. Rafi answers with an ordinary greeting, then lets Kai speak. The mission remains a task shared by competent adults, while young players learn what support sounds like.

The player chooses one checked observation to send with the greeting. Either shows the same ring explanation and the same local-view qualification. A conceptual globe can mark Bangladesh as part of the Earth connection; it cannot certify an uncomputed local sunrise. When the window closes, the receipt identifies the delivered packet. Kai keeps working with a memory that now includes a plan and other voices.

The player pins the note beside the present observation and labels it personal recollection. Ferreira reads it once, quietly. Her own memory of leaving the Moon does not answer every astronomical question either. Rafi saves the camera state before the next segment. This calm step matters: records are stored locally, so a later interruption cannot erase the experience or require the player to pretend to see it again.

The view screen drops. The guide light stays on. For a second Kai's hand closes around the lamp before he remembers to read the protected-service indicators. Atmosphere, circulation and garden minimums remain stable. The interruption belongs to camera feeder F2, not to the entire habitat.

The player calls the local checkback rehearsed earlier. Rafi answers. Amara points to the same isolation boundary used on the safe test board. The player isolates F2 and checks the cleared fault indication before resetting anything. A button pressed out of sequence offers the missing condition in words; it does not manufacture a lethal punishment.

Kai speaks the actions as they occur. The room never becomes bright enough to erase his fear, and it does not need to. After the protected sequence, he reconnects only the camera branch for its test. Ferreira remains nearby without taking over the player's task. A successful reset returns a view, but the important change is a repeatable method: stop, identify, isolate, verify and ask someone to stay on the channel.

scenes.title: Egress Is a Result
scenes.prose:
The camera image returns before the last observation gate. The player checks its time label, records egress and compares the recovered view with the saved ingress and ring frames. The interruption remains visible in the record. There is no need to pretend the camera never failed in order to report a successful observation.

Amara asks for the final energy check under the same teaching model. The player reconciles the one-time pump and camera allocations, the essential packages and the remaining margin. No extra fault penalty is silently charged for following the correct procedure. If an earlier setting needs revision, the checkpoint identifies that setting rather than demanding an entire chapter replay.

Kai places the lamp back in its clip without turning it into a trophy. He says he was afraid and completed the work anyway. Rafi repeats the part that made it possible: a plan, a known light and a crew who answered. The player saves the causal debrief, linking the protected design to the services that survived. Courage is recorded as supported action, not an emotion supposedly cured.

The next morning's solar image contains an active region worth monitoring. Rafi pins it to the calendar, then stops the player from drawing a line straight to a February storm date. A region is a reason to watch. It is not a precise month-ahead prediction of the next chapter.

The player builds a monitoring handover that names instruments, observations and who checks the next report. Cotton has leaves now. The garden's current generation has its own dates, and the preserved petal remains in the archive rather than reappearing on a living stem. Amara reconciles the protected founder reserve and the eleven unplanted vault specimens before the calendar advances.

A required montage moves through dated care, maintenance and ordinary meals. It shows what keeps an expedition alive between spectacular events without asking the player to wait through real weeks. Each short interaction checks a changed observation or hands over responsibility. February's alert arrives as new information after that work, not as proof of an impossible January forecast. The player opens the shared warning, with all five occupants present.

scenes.prose:
Breakfast stops when the new warning arrives. This time Rafi does not soften it with a joke or an apology. He puts the observations where everyone can see them and asks each specialist to read the part the others need. The player opens the source label before opening the forecast.

The chapter uses a clearly identified counterfactual replay: what if the powerful July 2012 solar event had struck the Moon? Its historical measurements inform the scenario; the fictional expedition date, three playable waves and game exposure are not presented as observed lunar damage. Rafi sets the warning beside the breakfast bowls. His hand is steady as he asks the others what the new evidence changes.

Rao confirms the last pre-isolation packet through a working Earth link. Ferreira then moves her chair away from the head of the table. She assigns operational planning to the cadets while retaining command responsibility. Kai asks for every observation before touching a setting. The player's first decision is what the evidence justifies, not how dramatic the warning sounds.

The plant chamber does not become an oxygen generator just because its leaves look healthy. Stored air, powered scrubbers and edible supplies remain explicit systems. Rafi places five seat markers on the shelter diagram. A missing marker leaves the readiness board incomplete even if the energy arithmetic looks attractive. scenes.title: One Plan, Not Four Good Intentions

Four proposed plans arrive at once. Kai wants power margin, Amara wants uninterrupted circulation, Mei wants warm roots, and Rafi wants complete shielding. Each sounds sensible alone. The player overlays them and finds the conflict: water borrowed for the shelter is water unavailable to the garden until the return operation.

The forecast shows six dark steps and no invented solar income. Current entry reserves belong to this chapter, after preparation costs; they are not April's old end-state copied forward. The player assembles one schedule using the established water, cargo and temperature rules. A complete baseline can protect five people, living crops and the thirty-seed reserve without an earned upgrade being a mandatory key.

Each proposed change updates a specific forecast: dose before transfer, plant stress after care, or remaining energy. The player must explain a rejected alternative before committing the integrated version. Ferreira asks whose objective was left outside. The answer has to be nobody's. Their plan is ready only when every role can trace its own dependency through the same six steps.

The player checks the seals against the thirty-seed record before latching the case.

At the wall, the forecast compares two water-return times. Draining early eases garden thirst but weakens a later exposure. Holding through the final sample preserves shielding, then returning the scheduled water protects the living plants. The player traces the order on a physical valve diagram before using the controls. Cargo bundles remain installed through the last exposure instead of disappearing under April's different shift schedule.

Rafi checks that every tool has a secured place. Mei touches the case once, then closes it. Protecting dry seeds and caring for living plants are related jobs with different conditions. The plan must do both. The player confirms the return-pump priority while the shelter remains open and preparation is still safe.

The readiness panel reaches its preparation threshold. Rafi stops discussing plans and begins the roll call. The player locates five people in the shelter and confirms each response through the local channel. A chair icon alone is not proof that someone reached it; the name, position and answer must agree.

Mei checks the sealed founder case while Amara verifies the atmosphere indicator. Kai confirms the protected electrical branch and the scheduled isolation of exposed radio hardware. Ferreira answers her own roll-call entry like everyone else. She does not remain outside for a heroic last photograph. The garden's instruments continue reporting through the local network; their pressure-safe enclosure is not opened.

The player closes the hatch and compares its two indications. A mismatch holds the step clock while the relevant check is repeated. Reading, caption hold and assisted input do not spend hidden oxygen. Once the compartment and roster agree, the first forecast becomes the first committed step. The shelter is a place where preparation becomes observable behaviour, and all five people remain visibly part of that behaviour.

The first committed step changes the ledger exactly as previewed. The player checks energy, atmosphere, food and the garden's local telemetry against the forecast, then states which differences would require intervention. The storm is not shown as luminous stones flying into the greenhouse. Its danger is communicated by instruments, procedure and the room's restrained sound.

A second step follows only after the player acknowledges the first. The chapter's six steps each represent seven-point-two scenario hours; the active gameplay does not ask anyone to sit still for that duration. A time card and changed system values communicate the interval. The main route spends its time on prediction, comparison and decision, not on an empty countdown.

The protected seed case remains sealed. One compartment indicator briefly invites inspection of its recorded sensor value, not opening it during exposure. Mei checks the local garden trace while Kai confirms the isolated exposed branch. Their reports meet at the same table. When the first wave ends, the player has a supported explanation for why the plan is holding.

In the lull, the player opens the final recovered recording. Its caption identifies a historical archive, already stored locally. Noor's voice does not cross the current storm or prove the Earth link is open. She is speaking from the old expedition's departure day.

She explains the name Alo: light left for someone who might bring it back. The Academy took its name from the last sunset she saw before leaving the Moon. The player places the log beside the first seed packet, the consented identity page and the current founder ledger. The mystery now has a complete chain, not one last invented password.

Mei holds Alo's pressed petal near its case without pretending it can hear. The reserve beside them contains descendants' possible futures, while the living garden contains present responsibilities. Kai asks what their own final report should say. The player selects a draft sentence, then supports it with an already checked action. Meaning cannot substitute for the remaining storm plan. When the log ends, the forecast still has four steps left, and the crew returns to them together.

scenes.prose:
The peak arrives in steps three and four. On the chart, the game exposure multiplier rises, but the prepared shielding still performs the job predicted for it. The player checks the complete effective shield rather than judging safety from a frightening graph shape. No glowing radiation animation tells the player to run outside.

Kai confirms each essential load before commitment. Amara updates five-person air and food draw. Mei checks the living crops and keeps the founder reserve separate. Rafi verifies that shielding cargo remains installed. A player who proposes an early drain sees its consequence in preview and can revise locally before the next step.

The tail occupies steps five and six. Only after the sixth exposure is sampled does the scheduled drain return water toward the garden. The baseline result matches the established chapter contract; earned modifiers, when present, are applied once and shown. No extra income appears in the dark. By the final line, the player can explain which earlier decisions mattered and why the same water could protect different needs at different times.

scenes.location: Aurora local network and uplink diagnostic

The storm steps end, but Rao does not answer. Kai hears Rafi clearly across the corridor, and the garden continues sending local data. The player must diagnose those facts before calling every radio broken. The failed path leads outward through the exposed Earth-uplink feedthrough.

The diagnostic compares local network pass, direct-dish path fail and feedthrough fail. A correct protected isolation did not guarantee that every exposed component would survive the authored incident. The game does not secretly blame the player for damage written into the chapter. Choosing a local-radio reset leaves the external failure unresolved; selecting the external branch directs the next test correctly.

Travel remains blocked until two below-threshold scenario readings, separated by the required interval, clear later exterior preparation. One reassuring sample is not enough. Amara records the second result and saves the relay-bypass diagram. The stable habitat retains local control, stored procedures and the reserve it needs for continued operation. Silence has a defined boundary. The player can now plan a repair without pretending an unanswered message reached Earth.

scenes.title: A Base That Can Wait Safely
scenes.location: Aurora maintenance and care planning desk

A radio repair cannot become an excuse to ignore the weeks before departure. Mei opens a required stable-operation board. The player must show how the station continues local care, planned food supply, atmosphere maintenance and scheduled observation while the direct Earth uplink remains unusable. This is not an unmentioned life-support emergency stretched across two months.

Dated records show which stores are available and which routine operations consume them. The long interval does not multiply April's seven-shift game recipe across every hour. It uses the campaign's explicit maintenance and ration ledger. The player rejects a draft that assumes an Earth reply delivered a missing instruction; that reply has never arrived. Stored procedures and local expertise supply the actual plan.

Cotton grows under its own recorded care. Current mustard plants carry generation labels rather than the original Alo's name alone. Amara checks the founder reserve without opening it, then compares the retained vault register. Three dated maintenance gates test changed observations before time advances. The spare controller from December comes out of its locker, still sealed and still carrying Kai's compatibility note. The player checks it against the Malapert service housing. A controller alone cannot connect a summit to a base hidden by terrain. The bypass needs an Aurora-to-summit path and a summit-to-Earth path.

Rafi lays three repeater sites along the surveyed road model. A straight line drawn over a ridge fails the simulator's obstruction check. The player adjusts the surveyed installation plan until neighbouring links are supported, while retaining the established safe road rather than inventing a shortcut. The final approach will test the actual chain again. A desktop plan is preparation, not proof of deployment.

At the bench, the player loads the spare battery, matches service connectors and runs a controlled known-content echo demonstration through the prepared local hardware. A wrong connector stays on the bench with an explanatory mismatch. Ferreira signs the isolation checklist; Kai labels the packed controller. The dated preparation ends with physical equipment and an intelligible route, so the finale will use things the player helped make ready.

Five names face two destination boards. Ferreira, Kai and Rafi take the rover. Mei and Amara remain at Aurora. The player assigns no invisible extra operator and sends no cadet to two places at once. Rafi reads the planned journey: twenty-four hours outward, three for repair, twenty-four back, with seventy-two hours of independent provisions.

Amara opens the home-night ledger. For the first thirty-three dark hours, two people will breathe at the base. The three travellers return for the final three hours before dawn. The player checks that change before signing either team's plan. A flat four-person copy from April would count the wrong people twice.

Mei and Kai exchange duplicate route and shelter checklists. He asks for the small guide light, and she points to its existing place in the schedule. No promise requires wasteful brightness. The player confirms packed equipment, local check-in markers and the stable preparation record. The calendar reaches departure only after those checks. On the surveyed road, the baseline rover starts with fourteen game units. Five cover outward travel and planned work, five cover the return, leaving four above the two-unit minimum. An earned long-range battery changes the entry capacity once and visibly. It never turns an unsafe slope into a permitted road or replaces the return check.

The player marks reserve that must remain unavailable for decorative loads. Kai points out that saving energy means little if the vehicle cannot safely reach the place where it will be spent. The forecast keeps distance, terrain and reserve on the same page. Only after the player explains the rejected shortcut does cruise begin along the supported route.

scenes.location: Aurora console and rover summit approach
scenes.pointOfView: Amara then Rafi at labelled cut
scenes.prose:
At Aurora, the player watches the garden forecast meet the first checked result. Amara verifies air, temperature and the open return path before acknowledging any field message. A working relay later cannot compensate for a neglected home system now. The scene keeps both responsibilities visible without letting one player move characters between sites.

A timestamped rover packet reports the final approach. The three road repeaters carry local traffic across the four required surface hops; the broken Earth uplink remains broken. The player checks sender, location and packet age. A stored earlier position is available as a comparison, making it possible to recognise why a stale acknowledgement would mislead the other team.

The viewpoint card then cuts to Rafi at the summit, exactly twenty-four scenario hours after departure. Ferreira and Kai are with him in the pressurised rover. The player has completed a complete outward leg and preserved home, not repaired Earth by implication. scenes.prose:
The controller crate opens beside the service housing its diagram promised. Kai recognises the note he wrote in December. The player checks the actual connectors and serial once more because preparation does not excuse verification at the point of use. Ferreira braces the service door while Rafi controls the tether.

The first command isolates power. The second verifies zero before the damaged controller is removed. A tempting reset control remains visible but cannot certify a safe replacement. The player follows the sequence through removal, compatible insertion and closed housing. Only then is power reconnected. Each step has a direct physical change rather than another decorative inspection.

Nothing sparks theatrically in the vacuum. The score stays quiet enough for the local checkbacks to be understood. When the controller powers, the antenna panel wakes with two unverified channels. Kai does not announce success yet. Months of care, the delivered spare and the restored road have made this moment possible, but the device still has to connect Aurora with Earth. The player has repaired a component and created the conditions for testing a system.

With the first leg checked, the player adjusts the Earth dish. The displayed bearings are labelled scenario values until surveyed geometry is verified in production. Strength alone is insufficient when the path remains obstructed; the panel pairs signal with an explicit blockage indication. An assisted preset and tap-confirm offer the same engineering result as the dials, without taking away story access or rewards.

The upcoming Aurora Earth-set handover appears as a planned window, not a reason to force fast motor input. Reading and accessibility settings pause the pressure. Ferreira reads the two-channel checklist while Rafi confirms the local path remains stable. Kai touches each verified label once. The relay's useful achievement is not pointing at a distant object. It is maintaining a route that can carry a message between people.

A nearly matching reply is available in the diagnostic preview, and the player must distinguish resemblance from equality.

A signal meter can be strong while content arrives incorrectly. Rafi checks that the returned characters match and that the acknowledgement belongs to this test rather than an old saved packet. The player then confirms the Earth channel separately. Two independent voice checks remain visible as required next steps, so a successful data echo does not silently stand in for a conversation.

At Aurora, Mei sees the verified route appear on the board. Her own garden forecast still needs its scheduled care; the radio did not refill the battery or reverse time. Amara sends a current telemetry packet, with the station's clock and five-person return plan attached. The network is now useful because the player can show where the information went and what came back. Only after that evidence does the transmit button invite a human voice.

scenes.prose:
The transmit control waits until both path checks are visible. The player confirms Aurora's voice, then Earth's. Rao identifies the restored route and leaves room on the channel. Only now does Noor choose to speak live: Hello, Aurora. This is Noor.

The picture cuts among the pressurised summit cabin, Aurora's table and a rooftop in Bangladesh. The Earth shot belongs to the fictional scene; it makes no unsupported claim about exact Moon phase or local visibility. The crew leaves pauses for radio delay. Nobody talks continuously from an unprotected lunar exterior.

Mei sends current garden telemetry and the preserved lineage photograph. Noor sees what reached her through the working path, not everything that happened during the blackout. She says the crew did what she could not. Ferreira answers that the seeds and the Academy made their work possible. The player selects a supported report sentence and lets each contributor remain named. This is a shared achievement, not a replacement for Noor or a redemption purchased by one heroic rescue. Before the call ends, Rafi reads the return departure time.

The player compares actual use with the whole-mission forecast, including the three-hour repair window. Arrival at Malapert never counted as the finish.

Three short route checks show the restored repeaters still supporting communication. They test new return observations rather than asking the player to repeat the outward puzzle without change. A stale outward timestamp is rejected when the player confirms a homebound position. Guided cruise can compress travel while preserving those decisions and the full fictional duration.

At Aurora, Amara receives the approaching packet and prepares the actual arrival transition. The airlock does not open because a cinematic needs a reunion. The player verifies the three returning names and pressure procedure. At 03:00 on 10 April, five lunar crew are physically home. The home ledger changes consumption for the final three dark hours. scenes.title: What We Grew
scenes.storyTime: 10 April 06:00, first light and complete epilogue
scenes.prose:
The viewing shutter waits where the first bloom once appeared. Before touching it, the player verifies the final records: five people safely home, thirty founder seeds protected, eleven unplanted vault specimens retained, stable pressure and temperature, and cotton alive. The checks describe an established garden that survived another seasonal dark window. Dawn will reveal it, not create it instantly.

Mei opens the shutter. Mustard descendants flower inside the pressurised room. Alo's petal remains beside the lineage label, and Tara's contribution appears beside Alo's. Noor watches through the restored screen. Cotton stands by the window, continuing the historical beginning represented by the 2019 seedling without pretending this fictional plant rewrites that real experiment.

The player takes the shared photograph and chooses a dedication supported by the completed work. Credits name both teams and the people who made their first chance possible. All central questions have answers before the ending closes. A brief post-credit still may show the closed MARS drawer as a future-story image; it adds no quest, collectible or required activity to this campaign. Continue returns to the safe completed garden.
